newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen offers eight state-run firms for sale.
newsitem.headline: Yemen offers eight state-run firms for sale.

text.p: Yemen on Monday offered eight troubled state-run enterprises for sale to the private sector in the southern port city of Aden as part of economic reforms.

"In line with the government's decision to sell and liquidate troubled public industrial enterprises, it has been decided to sell eight of them," said a public auction announcement, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
The companies produce goods ranging from leather items, garments, sweets and bread to iron and farming tools, it added.
It set April 4 as a deadline to receive bids.
It gave no further details and officials were not immediately available for comment.
Yemen said last February it had privatised three Aden-based tourist establishments, two hotels and a recreation club, under a 1995 plan to transfer state holdings in industries to private investors.

The government has made it a policy to call on foreign and local investors to participate in its privatisation programme, long advocated by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund as part of the impoverished country's economic reforms.
